about.title: San Luis Obispo Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: San Luis Obispo draws steady foot traffic downtown near Higuera Street and along shopping corridors close to Los Osos Valley Road, and property owners in these areas carry a responsibility to keep walkways, stairs, and entrances reasonably safe. When a spill, cracked pavement, poor lighting, or a hidden hazard causes a fall, the property owner or manager isn't automatically at fault — California law requires showing they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and any available surveillance footage from the store or building can make the difference in a claim. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly; we're a free service that connects you with an independent San Luis Obispo attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the evidence before it disappears, and explain your options. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a San Luis Obispo Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before it hurt you. An attorney knows how to gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish this.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Affects Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your share of blame but isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help present the facts fairly and push back against unfair blame-shifting.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in San Luis Obispo?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim under California law. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as the City of San Luis Obispo or SLO County, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's best to talk to an attorney as soon as possible so no deadline is missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a downtown San Luis Obispo shop or restaurant?
items.answer: Businesses along corridors like Higuera Street and Broad Street are expected to keep floors, entryways, and stairs reasonably safe for customers. If a hazard existed and the owner or staff knew, or should have known, about it and didn't address it, you may have grounds for a claim. An attorney can help request incident reports and any surveillance footage the business may have.

items.question: Will I still be able to recover money if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault, but you aren't automatically barred from recovering. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.
